units.la: Obtinebant eo tempore Alani & Vandali Africam; Visigothi Hispaniam, Franci & Burgundiones Gallias; Hunni vero reliquas Occidentalis Imperij Provincias: rabie incredibili universæ minitantes Italiæ. Romani hic suis rebus diffidentes, quum xx annorum intervallo decem jam habuissent Imperatores, variis & ipsos Bellis atque Seditionibus conflictatos & occisos; in maxima rerum omnium perturbatione & tumultu, Scythas, Albanos, Gothicasque quosdam Nationes in Italiam sui præsidio evocatas, in Societatem adscitas, Occasionem ante omnes alios Gothi avide arripientes, Italiam ingressi, tertiam Agrorum Partem ab Oreste Patritio, qui pro Augustulo Filio Imperium gubernabat, petunt: negantique se concessurum insidiantur; Odovacrem Herulum, qui quondam inter Italicos Milites Orestis Armiger fuerat, quum omnia pro ipsorum arbitrio se exsequuturu promisisset, Romanorum constituunt Principem. Is Augustulo Ravennæ anno Christi cccclxxv, decimo Kalendas Septembris abdicare iussô, Patreque ipsius Oreste quinto Kalendas eiusdem mensis Placentiæ occiso, stabilita Tyrannide, dominari longe lateque Italiæ coepit. Cum Augustulo igitur Imperium Pop. Romani Occidentale desiit. Gothorum enim & Langhardorum Regibus totam fere Italiam regio nomine obtinentibus, Imperatores deinceps in Occidente creari desierunt, usque ad Karolum Magnum Francorum Regem; fuitque in Occidente Interregnum annorum cccxxiv, mensiumque iv, usque ad annum i Imperij Karoli Magni.
units.tr: At that time the Alans and Vandals held Africa; the Visigoths held Spain; the Franks and Burgundians held the Gauls; while the Huns held the remaining provinces of the Western Empire, threatening Italy with incredible fury. The Romans, distrustful of their own affairs, though in a span of twenty years they had had ten emperors, who were themselves harassed by various wars and seditions and killed, in the greatest upheaval and tumult of all affairs, called in the Scythians, Alans and certain Gothic nations to their protection in Italy and admitted them into alliance. The Goths, eagerly seizing the opportunity before all others, entered Italy and demanded a third part of the fields from Orestes the Patrician, who governed on behalf of his son Augustulus. When he refused, they plotted against him, and they set up as prince of the Romans Odoacer the Herul, who had once been an armour-bearer of Orestes among the Italian soldiers, after he promised to carry out everything at their pleasure. He ordered Augustulus to abdicate at Ravenna in the year of Christ 475, on 23 August, and had his father Orestes killed at Placentia on 28 August. With tyranny established, he began to rule far and wide over Italy. So with Augustulus the Western Empire of the Roman people came to an end. For with the kings of the Goths and Lombards holding almost all of Italy under royal title, emperors ceased thereafter to be created in the West, until Charles the Great, king of the Franks. There was an interregnum in the West of 324 years and 4 months, until the first year of the reign of Charles the Great.

units.la: Fl. Odoacer Herulus, Gothorum Rex, post Augustulum Regis nomine Primus Romæ in Occidente regnavit. Annos Per idem tempus Ostrogothi, qui paullo ante post Attila mortem, cui servierat, Iltro traiecto, Imperatoris permissu, Thraciâ colere coeperat, adversus Romanos Orientales Theoderico Duce, arma sustulerant. Imperator Zeno, qui optime disponere prælentia callebat, Theodoricum potius, ut Italiam peteret, monet; & Odoacre Tyrano ciecto, Italiæ principarum sibi Ostrogothisque parare: illi id longe plurimum conducturum adfirmás præstanti ac Senatorio Viro (Patricius enim & Consularis factus erat Imperatoris Byzantini beneficio) ut Tyranno devicto, Romanis & Italicis ceteris imperitaret, quam secum, ut Imperatore tore, inconsideratius velit Armis decernere, ac tam dubium inire belli fortunæ discrimē. Theodericus Imperatoris persuasione ac cōsilio delectatus, ex Thracia Italiam versus iter cum universo Ostro-Gothorum populo suscepit. Quum in Italiam venisset, Odoacrem triplici prælio victum, postremo interfecit. Tum omnibus sibi conciliatis, Gothorum solus & Italicorum Imperium tenuit, Romani tamen Imperatoris nec Insignia, nec Nomen sibi defumsit; sed, quo ad vixit, Rex appellatus est. units.tr: Flavius Odoacer the Herul, king of the Goths, reigned in Rome in the West as the first to hold the royal title after Augustulus. At about the same time the Ostrogoths, who had shortly before, after the death of Attila whom they had served, crossed the Danube and begun to dwell in Thrace by the emperor's permission, took up arms against the Eastern Romans under their leader Theoderic. The Emperor Zeno, who knew well how to arrange present affairs, advised Theoderic rather to make for Italy, and, with Odoacer the tyrant removed, to win Italy and its chief cities for himself and the Ostrogoths. He assured him that this would greatly serve his purpose: a distinguished man of senatorial rank (for he had been made patrician and consul by the favour of the Byzantine emperor) should rule over the Romans and the rest of the Italians once the tyrant was defeated, rather than the emperor, being less prudent, should wish to settle matters with arms against him and enter upon so doubtful a risk of war's fortune. Theoderic, delighted by the emperor's persuasion and counsel, undertook the journey from Thrace towards Italy with the whole Ostrogothic people. When he had come into Italy, he defeated Odoacer in three battles and finally killed him. Then, having won over everyone to himself, he held sole rule over the Goths and the Italians; yet he did not assume the insignia or the name of Roman emperor, but, as long as he lived, was called king. | II | CCCCXCIV | Theodericus Strabo Amales, son of Theoderic, grandson of Valamirus. units.la: Prælio victus à Belisario & Narse, præstantissimis Iustiniani Augusti Ducibus, occisus est; Gothique omnes Italia pulsi circa mensem Maium anno Christi ɔliii. Bello confecto, Gothisque Italia omni exactis, ipsa cum Insulis Sicilia, Sardinia & Corsica Imperio Orientali est attributa; atq; in Victoriæ præmium Narsi ab Imperatore administranda est concessa.
units.tr: Defeated in battle by Belisarius and Narses, the most outstanding generals of the Emperor Justinian, he was killed; and all the Goths were driven out of Italy around the month of May in the year of Christ 553. With the war concluded and the Goths expelled from all of Italy, Italy itself, together with the islands of Sicily, Sardinia and Corsica, was assigned to the Eastern Empire; and the administration of it was granted by the emperor to Narses as the reward of victory.

units.la: Italia Orientali Imperio concessa: Narses Romanorum Procerum invidia exagitatus, à quibus apud Iustinum Imp. accusatus fuerat, quum ex Italia revocatus esset, contumeliis Sophiæ Augustæ irritatus, Langbardos, qui tunc cum Hunnis Pannoniam incolebant, quorumque precipue auxilio Gothos Italiæ finibus expulerat, in Italiam evocavit: quam illi Duce Alboino ingressi omnem fere occuparunt; Præsidijsque Græci Imperatoris pulsis, annos ccvi tenuerunt: quo temporis intervallo totam Italiam, præter Urbem, in Ditionem suam sub Regibus xxiii redegerunt.
units.tr: Italy having been granted to the Eastern Empire, Narses, harassed by the envy of the Roman nobles, by whom he had been accused before the Emperor Justin, was recalled from Italy; irritated by the insults of the Augusta Sophia, he summoned into Italy the Lombards, who then dwelt with the Huns in Pannonia and whose chief help had enabled him to drive the Goths from the borders of Italy. Under their leader Alboin they entered Italy and occupied nearly all of it; having expelled the garrisons of the Greek emperor, they held it for 206 years. During this period of time they reduced all Italy, except the city, under their power, under 23 kings.

units.la: Alboinus Andoini F. Primus in Italia Langbardorum Rex. Regnavit Iustinus Iunior Augustus Exarchatum Ravennæ instituit; sicque mortuo Fl. Narsete Italiæ Duce, Fl. Longinus reliquam eius partem, quam Langbardi primo impetu occupare non potuerant, pro Imperatore Constantinopolitano, locata Ravennæ Imperij Sede, sub Exarchi nomine obtinuit.
units.tr: Alboin, son of Audoin, first King of the Lombards in Italy, reigned. The Emperor Justin the Younger established the exarchate of Ravenna; and thus, when Flavius Narses, governor of Italy, had died, Flavius Longinus held the rest of that part which the Lombards had not been able to seize at the first onslaught, on behalf of the Emperor of Constantinople, with the seat of empire placed at Ravenna, under the title of exarch.

MDLXXIII Clephe ab Servo suo, Interregnum fuit in regno Langbardorum annorum x; in quo xxxvi Langbardorum Duces Regnum singillatim per singulas Vrbes administrarunt: inter quos Zabanus Ticinum: Alboinus, Mediolanum; Valarus, Bergomum; Alahus, Brixiam; Cous, Tridentum; Gisulphus, Forum-Iulij; & alij xxx Duces reliquas Vrbes obtinuerunt.
units.tr: Cleph, second King of the Lombards in Italy. After Cleph was killed by his servant at Pavia about 1 April 573, there was an interregnum in the kingdom of the Lombards for ten years; during which thirty-six Lombard dukes ruled the kingdom separately, city by city: among them Zabanus at Ticinum, Alboin at Mediolanum, Valaris at Bergomum, Alachis at Brixia, Cosus at Tridentum, Gisulf at Forum Iulii; and thirty other dukes held the remaining cities.
